job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

response.passage: Many people often confuse the internet with the World Wide Web, but they are actually quite different. The internet is a vast, global network of millions of interconnected computers, servers, and devices linked by physical cables, including massive ones running under the ocean. Think of the internet as the physical road system that allows data to travel. In contrast, the World Wide Web is just one of the services that runs on top of this network, like a library of pages you visit using a browser. When you send a photo to a friend, it is not sent as one single block. Instead, the data is broken into tiny pieces called packets that travel independently across various paths before reassembling at the destination. Furthermore, the internet is not a magical space; every device connected to it, from your laptop to your smart TV, is assigned a unique numerical IP address to identify it. While Wi-Fi provides a wireless link to your local router, it is merely the final step of the connection. The actual internet relies on a complex infrastructure of wires and servers that span the entire globe, managed by many different organizations rather than a single entity.
response.summary: The internet is a global physical network of connected devices, while the World Wide Web is a service that runs on top of it. Data moves across this network in small packets, and every connected device uses an IP address to communicate.
